papers.title: The Wild West of Nomenclature, Definitions, and Methodologies in Rodent Sleep Scoring.
papers.summary: This Perspective reviews the inconsistent terminology, definitions, and methodologies used in rodent sleep scoring, illustrating how epoch duration and bout initiation/continuation/termination criteria alter sleep-stage assignment, bout counts and durations, transition frequency, and apparent fragmentation or consolidation. It proposes consistent terminology, explicit operational definitions, and minimum reporting practices to improve reproducibility and cross-study comparison.

papers.title: Nucleus reuniens gates selective hippocampal-prefrontal interactions during NREM sleep
papers.summary: Using in vivo electrophysiology in rats during NREM sleep, the authors identified ripple-like activity in nucleus reuniens (~120 Hz, ~45 ms) that phase-locked to hippocampal sharp wave-ripples and mPFC ripples and was associated with thalamic spiking. HC-mPFC ripple coupling mainly occurred with co-occurring RE ripples, suggesting RE ripples gate hippocampal-prefrontal interactions during sleep.

papers.title: Repeated self-administered EEG recordings enable longitudinal measurement of brain activity at home
papers.summary: Five participants completed repeated self-administered at-home EEG sessions (resting state and auditory oddball with/without cognitive load) using a four-channel consumer device and captured expected alpha, theta, and event-related response signatures. Aggregating sessions improved reliability, with split-half reliability of the N1-like response rising from r = .22 for one session to r = .76 for seven sessions per half.

papers.title: The aging human brain exhibits reduced hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves during sleep.
papers.summary: This study imaged large-scale cerebrospinal fluid flow and hemodynamics during nighttime sleep in young (18-39 years) and older (60-84 years) adults, finding reduced sleep-dependent CSF flow in older adults linked to lower EEG slow wave power, decreased global hemodynamic oscillations, and gray matter atrophy. Sensory and vasoactive stimuli indicated that both neural and cerebrovascular changes contribute to the disruption.

papers.title: Mutations in antimicrobial peptides differently affect sleep and plasticity.
papers.summary: Drosophila antimicrobial peptide (AMP) mutants were characterized for sleep and plasticity, showing reduced sleep, longer sleep latency, and altered arousal thresholds, with the double Mtk/Drs (Group C) mutant most impaired and exhibiting exaggerated sleep rebound. Group C mutants retained normal learning and memory despite sleeping least and had lower synapse abundance, while other AMP mutants showed sleep and memory deficits that were reversible with sleep enhancement.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.summary: This study combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG, and personalized dense bilateral frontoparietal fNIRS in healthy young adults, plus an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset, to characterize cortical hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states. Slow-frequency (0.002-0.1 Hz) HbO power rose in N1 and attenuated across N2/N3 in HbO, HbR, and fMRI, REM showed re-emergence of very-low-frequency (<0.01 Hz) power, and higher-frequency (0.15-0.5 Hz) oscillations were enhanced during NREM sleep.

papers.title: Effects of Ambulatory Blood Pressure Monitoring During Polysomnography on Sleep Indices and EEG Power.
papers.summary: In a balanced two-night crossover of 72 nominally healthy adults with ABPM on one randomly assigned night, both ABPM and first-night effect were associated with lower composite sleep quality index, with ABPM linked to higher light-sleep and lower N3-sleep percentages and higher whole-night relative theta power. Of 655 ABPM measurements beginning during sleep, 60.3% contained at least one arousal detection within the 2-min window.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.summary: The paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network that splits epochs into overlapping patches, uses a dynamic modal re-weighting module to weight EEG/EOG signals per patch, and applies a bidirectional Mamba encoder with positional encoding for cross-epoch context. On Sleep-EDF and ISRUC it reportedly outperformed state-of-the-art methods, with ablations demonstrating the effectiveness of its modules.

papers.title: Effects of BL Exposure on Circadian Rhythms and Rhythm-Related Disorders.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on the bidirectional effects of blue light (BL) exposure on circadian rhythms and related disorders, outlining molecular mechanisms and disease pathways. It highlights that inappropriately timed BL may disrupt circadian rhythms and contribute to sleep, mood, and neurodegenerative disorders, while appropriately timed BL interventions may improve circadian alignment, though causal pathways remain unestablished.

papers.title: Light-induced melatonin suppression in school-aged children before and during camping: associations with circadian phase and daytime light exposure
papers.summary: In 21 school-aged children, evening light-induced melatonin suppression did not differ significantly before versus after roughly two weeks of natural light-dark cycle exposure during camp (p = 0.21). Greater suppression was associated with later DLMO pre-camp (rho = 0.49) and with lower same-day daytime illuminance during camp (rho = -0.58), indicating large interindividual variation linked to circadian phase and recent light exposure.

papers.title: The Circadian Diet in Age-Related Neurodegeneration: Nutrient Timing, Sleep, and Mitochondrial Mechanisms.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines chrononutrition in age-related neurodegeneration, integrating evidence from cellular, animal, and human studies on meal timing, sleep, and mitochondrial mechanisms. It concludes that while experimental findings provide mechanistic plausibility, metabolic improvements have not translated into demonstrated neuroprotection, and adequately powered trials are needed before a circadian diet can be established as disease-modifying.

papers.title: Epilepsy at the Airport.
papers.summary: This retrospective study reviewed 242 Epilepsy Rapid Access Clinic attendees over 19 months and identified 18 patients with air travel-related seizures, all bilateral tonic-clonic, with clustering in departure terminals particularly before morning flights and sleep deprivation as a common trigger. The findings suggest that patients with idiopathic generalised epilepsy may be at higher risk and that targeted counselling on modifiable risk factors could reduce risk.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Intensive Continuous Theta Burst Stimulation Over the Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex in Insomnia Disorder:A Randomized Sham-Controlled Trial.
papers.journal: The primary care companion for CNS disorders
papers.summary: This randomized sham-controlled trial gave 30 adults with insomnia disorder 21 sessions of continuous theta burst stimulation over the right dorsolateral prefrontal cortex or sham cTBS, with both groups improving on all sleep outcomes without significant group×time interactions. Active cTBS produced a significant, large advantage in health-related quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF, P=.002, ηp2=0.242) and was safe and well tolerated.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that low-friction, high-adherence passive sleep-tracking devices, such as smart rings, may offer advantages for longitudinal monitoring of neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's despite lower accuracy than gold-standard methods. It posits that long-term statistical benefits from detecting within-person changes and increased sampling frequency may offset accuracy-adherence trade-offs.

papers.title: Integrating Chronophysiological and Bioinformatic Perspectives on Nesfatin-1, Circadian Feeding Rhythms, and Cortisol Regulation.
papers.summary: This review integrates chronophysiological and bioinformatic perspectives on nesfatin-1, circadian feeding rhythms, and cortisol regulation, synthesizing rodent and cell studies and performing in silico protein-association analysis. It identifies an evidence gap regarding the 24-hour temporal profile of nesfatin-1 in humans and its phase relationship with cortisol, calling for controlled time-resolved human studies.

papers.title: Cannabinol for Sleep and Insomnia: A Critical Narrative Review and an Olive-Derived Polyphenol Combination Hypothesis.
papers.summary: This critical narrative review evaluated CBN-specific sleep trials and found that primary sleep-quality and sleep-maintenance outcomes were not consistently positive, with dose-ranging signals multiplicity-sensitive and no optimal dose identified; at 300 mg, an acute insomnia trial showed selected secondary sleep benefits alongside next-day vigilance and simulated-driving concerns. It proposed an olive-derived polyphenol combination only as an untested hypothesis requiring exposure-informed investigation, not therapeutic endorsement.

papers.title: Long Sleep Duration and Multimorbidity in Older U.S. Adults: A Dose-Response Analysis of NHANES 2017-March 2020.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional analysis of 2998 community-dwelling U.S. adults aged ≥60 years from NHANES 2017–March 2020, long sleep ≥9 h was associated with multimorbidity (aOR 1.65, 95% CI 1.22–2.25) with a J-shaped dose-response, whereas short sleep was not. The authors interpret long sleep as a marker of accumulated disease burden rather than an actionable risk factor given the cross-sectional design.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Related Characteristics and Adiposity in Relation to CAP-Defined Hepatic Steatosis Among Shift and Non-Shift Workers: A Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In a pilot study of 436 tea-factory workers, CAP-defined hepatic steatosis and CAP values did not differ significantly by shift-work status, and CAP was strongly correlated with anthropometric and adiposity indices (e.g., waist circumference, abdominal volume index, BMI, body fat mass; all rs = 0.66). Social jetlag, eating jetlag, sleep duration, and PSQI score were not independently associated with CAP, and waist circumference/AVI discriminated steatosis best in men while BMI performed best in women.

papers.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder.
papers.summary: Combining clinical assessments in BD and major depressive disorder patients with sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mice, this translational study found elevated peripheral creatine and hepatic GAMT expression; exogenous creatine recapitulated manic-like phenotypes, whereas β-GPA or subdiaphragmatic vagotomy ameliorated them. Peripherally derived creatine acted via IL-1α-mediated inflammatory signaling and hippocampal MMP19 upregulation, delineating a vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in bipolar disorder.

papers.title: Probable REM sleep behavior disorder and reduced cerebrospinal fluid 5-hydroxyindoleacetic acid levels in Parkinson's disease.
papers.summary: In a retrospective study of 85 Parkinson's disease patients, probable RBD was associated with lower CSF 5-HIAA levels (9.9 ± 3.3 vs 14.5 ± 6.9 ng/mL, p < 0.001) and lower MIBG H/M ratios, with the 5-HIAA association persisting after adjustment for age, sex, and disease duration (β = -0.33, p = 0.01). Mediation analysis indicated the MIBG H/M ratio statistically accounted for part of this association.

papers.title: Postoperative Delirium Across the Perioperative Pathway: A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Maturity and Implementation Priorities.
papers.summary: Structured narrative review synthesizing evidence on postoperative delirium across the perioperative pathway, classifying prevention and treatment strategies by clinical maturity. Reports that multicomponent non-pharmacological prevention has the most consistent support, while no single anesthetic technique, EEG target, blood-pressure threshold, or pharmacological agent consistently prevents POD.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.summary: Comparative machine-learning analysis of pre-recorded EEG data from a stress-inducing experiment evaluating Hjorth parameters, spectral features, and fractal-dimension measures for stress classification. Hjorth activity, frontal beta asymmetry, and the gamma/theta ratio were among the most frequently selected features, and combined feature spaces outperformed conventional spectral features alone.

papers.title: Efficacy of Digital Health Interventions for Insomnia: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
papers.summary: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 44 randomized controlled trials (n=10,521) evaluating digital health interventions for insomnia across eight sleep outcomes. DHIs significantly improved insomnia severity (SMD -0.91) and sleep efficiency (SMD 0.59), but wide prediction intervals crossing the null and very low-to-moderate GRADE certainty indicate the evidence remains exploratory.

papers.title: Cortical Network Alterations and Treatment-Induced Reorganization in Panic Disorder: A Longitudinal High-Density EEG Study.
papers.summary: Used 128-channel resting-state high-density EEG in 52 drug-naive panic disorder patients and 43 controls, plus 6-week venlafaxine follow-up, to characterize source-level functional connectivity and network topology. Baseline alpha-band hyperconnectivity and reduced theta/delta connectivity distinguished groups (SVM accuracy 86.32%), and treatment was accompanied by increased alpha global efficiency and small-worldness and enhanced delta fronto-temporal connectivity.

papers.title: Sleep Disturbances in Female Military Personnel: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review screened 6,839 records and included 19 studies on sleep disturbances in female military personnel, finding greater vulnerability to insomnia onset, recurrence, and physiological dysregulation compared with male personnel. It identified 11 multilayered biological, psychological, socio-environmental, and structural risk factors and calls for tailored sleep hygiene interventions.

papers.title: Association of Self-Reported Sleep and Circadian Variability and Moral Judgements and Decision-Making.
papers.summary: Observational online survey of 109 healthy adults (18–39 years) examined associations of self-reported sleep and circadian factors with moral and social judgements. Greater online vigilantism and aversion to causing/witnessing harm were associated with earlier chronotype, higher sleep regularity, and less social jetlag (r > 0.20), while dictator-game generosity showed no significant association.

papers.title: Pregnancy-Recognized Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Maternal-Fetal Outcomes: A Narrative Review of Gestational Rhinitis, Upper-Airway Mechanisms, and Treatment Evidence.
papers.summary: Structured narrative review examining pregnancy-recognized obstructive sleep apnea, gestational rhinitis as a potential upper-airway contributor, and treatment evidence. Observational associations with hypertensive disorders and preterm birth are confounded by obesity, and a 2024 meta-analysis found CPAP associated with lower gestational hypertension (RR 0.65) and preeclampsia (RR 0.70) risk.

papers.title: Spontaneous Parturition at Term Is Governed by Endogenous Circadian Rhythms Rather Than Geophysical or Meteorological Factors: A Historical Cohort Study.
papers.summary: Historical cohort study of 21,538 spontaneous term singleton deliveries (1998-2022) testing lunar phase, barometric pressure, and heat associations with labor onset and premature rupture of membranes. No lunar or meteorological effects were found, whereas spontaneous deliveries showed a robust endogenous circadian peak at midday.

papers.title: Systemic influences on blood-brain barrier integrity - narrative review of insights from MRI.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes human in vivo MRI evidence on extracerebral/systemic conditions affecting blood-brain barrier permeability, finding the most reproducible impairment in hypertension, moderate evidence in systemic lupus erythematosus and long COVID, and suggestive associations with several other conditions. Systemic inflammation is identified as a common mechanistic pathway, with heterogeneity in imaging methods limiting cross-study comparability.

papers.title: Genetic Variants, Lifestyle Factors and Changes in Body Fat Percentage in Young Adults: An Exploratory Prospective Study.
papers.summary: This exploratory prospective study examined associations of eight obesity-associated polymorphisms and lifestyle exposures with change in body fat percentage over ~1.9 years in 84 young adults. Few associations were detected and most did not survive FDR correction, though greater body fat gain was linked to FTO rs1421085 T allele, lower vegetable intake, and longer sleep duration.

papers.title: Stress, Depression, and Purpose-Specific Use of Dietary Supplements and Over-the-Counter Preparations: A Cross-Sectional Study of 120,000 Polish Adults.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional web survey of 120,000 Polish adults, purpose-specific supplement/OTC use (mood, sleep, memory) rose along a gradient of psychological burden, with lifetime depression diagnosis associated with mood-product use (aOR 2.53) and OTC self-medication without reduced primary-care contact. Multivitamin and hair/skin use stayed flat, and associations replicated across age and sex strata (E-values 4.3–9.5).

papers.title: Lesion-directed quantitative EEG after reperfusion therapy is associated with malignant cerebral edema and functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of 49 anterior-circulation ischemic stroke patients, a lesion-directed alpha-to-delta ratio measured within 72 h after reperfusion was associated with functional outcomes, and combined with EEG timing showed good discrimination for malignant cerebral edema (optimism-corrected AUC 0.889). The association with 90-day independence was attenuated after adjusting for admission NIHSS.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.summary: This study evaluated a multi-domain EEG decoding framework combining time-frequency, functional and effective connectivity features with subject-specific calibration for recognizing four self-imagined emotions in 38 participants. PLV-based SVM features reached 97.0% accuracy under pooled cross-validation and 95.0% with 75% target-subject calibration, but leave-one-subject-out accuracy fell to 25-30%, indicating limited cross-subject generalization.

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.summary: The authors propose KimiFormer, a lightweight hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw wearable EEG, using a spatio-temporal stemming module and combined linear/full attention. It achieved 95.5% accuracy on the EEG Violence Dataset (97.0% under 10-fold CV) with 3.2M parameters and 15.64 ms latency, but subject-independent performance on the external DREAMER dataset remained near chance.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID syndrome: a scoping review of current evidence in adults.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review of 11 studies found evidence suggesting an association between obstructive sleep apnea and long COVID, with proposed mechanisms including intermittent hypoxia, systemic inflammation, autonomic dysregulation, sleep fragmentation, and circadian disturbance, though the direction and causality remain uncertain and evidence on OSA treatment effects is limited.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet, Physical Activity, and Sleep in Endometriosis: An Age-Comparable Case-Control Study with Exploratory Machine Learning Discrimination.
papers.summary: An age-comparable case-control study of 177 women found no difference in Mediterranean diet adherence or physical activity between endometriosis cases and controls after age adjustment and multiple-testing correction; only lower sofrito intake survived correction, and machine-learning discrimination (AUC 0.933) reflected concurrent symptoms rather than nutrition.

papers.title: High-Flow Nasal Oxygen and Desaturation During Deep Sedation for Colonoscopy in Patients at Increased Respiratory Risk: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
papers.summary: A propensity score-matched retrospective cohort of patients with OSA/high STOP-BANG undergoing deep sedation for colonoscopy found desaturation in 12.7% with high-flow nasal oxygen versus 22.5% with Venturi mask (matched OR 0.53, 95% CI 0.23–1.23; p=0.211), an imprecise estimate with insufficient power and residual confounding.

papers.title: The interplay of exercise, immunity, and suboptimal health in college students: an integrative narrative review with public health implications.
papers.summary: This integrative narrative review examines how different exercise types affect immune function, chronic low-grade inflammation, and suboptimal health status in college students, summarizing proposed mechanisms such as myokine-mediated anti-inflammatory signaling and immune cell mobilization while critiquing study-design and measurement limitations and offering public health implications.

papers.title: Reversal of photoperiodic flowering in temperate grasses rewired light inputs and floral outputs of the circadian clock.
papers.summary: Using comparative transcriptomics and functional principal component analysis of diel gene expression in short-day-flowering Nassella pubiflora and long-day-flowering Oloptum miliaceum, this study found that the reversal from long-day to short-day flowering involved divergence in relatively few floral integrator, light-signalling, and circadian clock target genes rather than widespread changes to core clock gene expression.

papers.title: From Risk to Resilience: A Narrative Synthesis of Protective Factors and Proposed Mechanisms in Bias-Based Bullying Among Youth (2016-2026).
papers.summary: A theory-informed narrative synthesis of 59 studies (2016–2026) found protective factors against bias-based bullying across individual, interpersonal, and institutional levels; individual strengths more often reduced harm than exposure, relational and institutional resources were more frequently protective, and no single factor protected all youth, with protection weaker under cumulative exposure.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
